sentence: This project develops imaging and analysis methods that make multispectral fluorescence imaging more accurate and consistent for measuring disease-related markers.
This project tests how well artificial intelligence tools interpret 3D mammography screening and estimates the long-term benefits, harms and costs of using them.
This project uses human stem cells to find out why some people's genes make them more likely to suffer heart damage from doxorubicin.
This project studies how yeast and human cells build mitochondrial membranes and the machinery that makes proteins in mitochondria.
This project maps gene activity and chromatin accessibility in single cell nuclei of trigeminal ganglion tissue from people with and without migraine.
This project studies how plasminogen, a protein in blood, moves small RNAs to macrophages and affects gene expression.
This project screens natural product extracts for molecules that keep prostate cancer from progressing to an advanced stage.
This project uses computational tools to find which genes and genetic variants raise the risk of asthma and how they affect cells.
This project uses protein structure to improve chimeric antigen receptor T cells that work against acute myeloid leukemia.
This project supports pilot projects on stem cells and aging, regenerative medicine and age-related diseases.
This project uses a cell village platform and engineered heart tissue to study how genetic variants lead to heart damage from doxorubicin.
This project builds a charge detection mass spectrometer that can quickly measure very large molecular and subcellular assemblies.
This project tries to find out what causes pulmonary veno-occlusive disease and tests possible therapeutics in animal models.
This project tests whether base edited stem cells and chimeric antigen receptor T cells can clear the HIV reservoir in non-human primates.
This project studies how Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, a foodborne pathogen, is maintained and transmitted locally.
This project studies how two groups of proteins regulate the expression of specific genes and the balance of silent heterochromatin.
This project studies how naked mole-rats keep their brains resilient despite a genetic vulnerability to benzodiazepine resistance.
This project studies how gene activity and chromatin changes in brain reward regions relate to opioid use disorder in humans.
This project sets up a mass spectrometry system to measure proteins in large numbers of clinical samples.
This project develops a deep learning framework that adds histological traits to systems genetics to find genes that modify complex diseases.
